description_full: Intuit Inc. provides financial management, payments and capital, compliance, and marketing products and services in the United States. The company operates in two segments: Global Business Solutions and Consumer. Its Global Business Solutions segment provides QuickBooks services, which include financial and business management online services, desktop software, payroll solutions, time tracking, merchant payment processing and bill pay solutions, checking accounts, and financing services for small and mid-market businesses; and Mailchimp, a marketing automation and customer relationship management. The Consumer segment provides TurboTax, a do-it-yourself and assisted income tax preparation products and services; Credit Karma, a personal finance solution that provides recommendations for credit card, home, auto, and personal loan, and insurance products; online savings and checking accounts; and access to its credit scores and reports, credit and identity monitoring, credit report dispute, credit building tools, debt pay-down assistance, credit card rewards optimization, and connected account capabilities. This segment also offers ProTax offerings which include Lacerte, ProSeries, and ProFile desktop tax-preparation software products; and ProConnect Tax Online, electronic tax filing service, and bank products and related services. It sells products and services through direct sales channels, multichannel shop-and-buy experiences, online application stores, and partner and other channels. Intuit Inc. has a strategic collaboration with Aprio, LLP to develop AI-powered solutions designed to help identify tax planning opportunities, benchmark business performance, improve financial visibility, and support more informed decision-making across industries, including construction, dental, wealth management, and tax. Intuit Inc. was founded in 1983 and is headquartered in Mountain View, California.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 18K people. Revenue per employee of $1.2M ranks in the top quartile among Technology peers, improving at 12%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $466K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $111K per employee reflects an ownership culture. financial_summary: Intuit Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $91.3B market cap on $21.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years and +16% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 10% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $8.7B in free cash flow — roughly 40 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.94× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -11.6% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.5× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 23× is fortress-like.
Management returns a meaningful 7.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.4% of the shares.

sector_headwinds.text: Volatile returns on capital suggest the moat is narrower than a snapshot ROIC implies
Insiders are overwhelmingly selling (100% sell ratio) — the people who know the business want less of it
Significant goodwill (38% of assets) from past acquisitions — a soft asset a conservative appraisal discounts to zero
Technology sector lagging the market significantly, underperforming by 7% over 3 months
Elevated sector volatility (35% annualized) adds uncertainty
Late-cycle dynamics increase the probability of a slowdown
Antitrust and platform-regulation risk — the larger the network effect, the larger the regulatory target on its back, and a single consent decree can reset the moat.
AI disruption of existing software moats — incumbents with durable margins face commoditisation as AI-native competitors replicate features at a fraction of the R&D cost.
Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sector_tailwinds: Operating margins 20% above sector median — the quantitative trace of pricing power
Shares offer a 24% margin of safety against estimated fair value
Piotroski score 7/9 — financials improving across profitability, leverage and efficiency
Altman Z comfortably in the safe zone — a fortress balance sheet on this measure
14 consecutive years of dividend payments — an operating record that makes the dividend claim credible
Healthy payout ratio leaves room for both dividend growth and reinvestment

sect: Its 27% operating margin runs 20pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.17x).
It accounts for 0.5% of sector revenue and 0.6% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 55% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 11% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 50% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 51% and a beta of 1.09, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.07 vs 5y 1.12), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $1.1B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 36% in the 2020 crash, 44% in the 2022 bear market and 37% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 24% below its DCF fair value of $451, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 36%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $342 to $605 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 20.7 vs 26.7 and P/FCF 10.5 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 57% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 9.5% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The 31 covering analysts target $408 on average, 19% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 15% earns above the cost of capital of 9.7%, but the 5pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.78).
It converts 40% of revenue into free cash flow, or 31% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is mixed: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.94x, but high accruals (-11.6% of assets).
ROE of 24% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
It spends 15.7% of revenue on R&D and 9.6% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.5x net debt to EBITDA ($4.7B of cash against $7.7B of debt), with interest covered 23.0x.
Goodwill makes up 38% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 14.3% over 3 years, 17.4% over 5 years and 16.4% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 31% of profits supports about 4.7% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 22.1% a year over five years.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 0.8% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 48, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.4%, and institutions hold 93%.
It returns 7.4% a year to shareholders (5.9% in buybacks and 1.6% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 14 consecutive years, raising it 15.8% a year over the last five.
people: With about 18,600 employees, each generates about $1.2M of revenue, 3.1x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 12.1% a year.
That works out to $466K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.9M (3x revenue per employee).
